newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh fears huge shortfall in sugar output.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh fears huge shortfall in sugar output.

text.p: Bangladesh, facing dwindling sugarcane supplies, fears a 150,000 tonne shortfall in sugar production in the 1996/97 financial year (July-June), the Financial Express said on Wednesday.
It quoted government officials as saying that the state-run Bangladesh Sugar and Food Corporation, anticipating a shortfall, was preparing to import 150,000 tonnes of sugar.
An official of the corporation, who declined to be identified, confirmed Bangladesh was facing a shortfall but added he was unable to give details immediately.
The newspaper said farmers were refusing to sell sugarcane to the factories at a government fixed price of 40 taka per maund (37 kg).
"They (farmers) are not interested in our offers and instead produce molasses for higher returns," the newspaper quoted a corporation official as saying.
It said farmers made 60 taka per maund if they sold molasses for smuggling into Burma and India.
The government had set a target of 215,000 tonnes of sugar production this year anticipating that 4.5 million tonnes of sugarcane would be available to factories.
But officials said only 1.12 million tonnes of sugarcane had been available at the mills until January 20. The crushing season ends in March.
Bangladesh consumes roughly 300,000 tonnes of sugar a year while domestic output ranges between 200,000 and 225,000 tonnes. The rest is imported.
